note: Divergence ratchets and depth floors for scripts/flix-spec-conformance.mjs. Lower a ratchet or raise a floor as the grammar improves; never move either the other way without saying why in the commit message. The measurement is only comparable against the flix-spec inputs recorded below -- a different pin or fixture revision is a different question, not a regression. Measure with flix-spec checked out at tag `v` + `measuredAt.flixSpecArtifact` (v0.77.2); `flixSpecPin` is the Flix tag that flix-spec release pins, not a flix-spec tag. scripts/flix-spec-conformance.mjs refuses a checkout whose artifact version, pin, vocabulary digests or fixture revision differ from `measuredAt`; pass --remeasure to measure a new release. Three ratchets, one per derived lane: `divergences` gates structure modulo error recovery, `recoveryDivergences` gates error-recovery shape on its own, and `diagnosticDivergences` gates accept/reject agreement. Each lane also has a depth floor (`depthFloor`, `recoveryDepthFloor`, in percent), because unmapped nodes are skipped rather than compared: agreement once fell from 122 to 107 when the mapping set was completed, while depth rose 84% to 90%. A divergence count that falls together with depth is the number to distrust, and the floor is what fails the build on it.

oracle_conformance.comment: Current, against flix-spec 0.77.2 (Flix v0.77.0, 147 fixtures): 86 divergences, 106/147 fixtures agree, depth 93%. What remains is mostly long-standing modelling differences -- Datalog query/inject shapes, schema and type-operator details, anonymous classes, error-recovery-adjacent lexical fixtures -- plus the leaf difference on the negative law fixture, where tree-sitter's ERROR keeps `lawful` as a child and the reference's ErrorTree holds only a token. The 17 unmapped nodes are aliased_name (10), argument (3), literal_pattern (2), associated_type_definition and debug_interpolation. History: 61 at flix-spec 0.75.8 (138 fixtures). Moving to 0.77.1 measured 102 -- nine new fixtures and per-occurrence transparency, a different question rather than a regression -- and a map fix (java_qualified_name in ignored) took it to 101. Grammar work for Flix v0.77.0 (use package paths, effect type parameters, generic operations kept whole) lowered it to 85; removing the retired law syntax set it at 86.

recovery_conformance.comment: Current: 55 divergences over the 28 fixtures whose reference tree contains a recovery marker, 6/28 agree, depth 67%. The dominant disagreement is diagnosed in flix-spec's docs/CONFORMANCE.md: both parsers reject `1_`, and they disagree about where the error is. One divergence remains by design: for a spaced package `::` the reference wraps the separator in an ErrorTree inside UsesOrImports.Package, while this grammar parses both spellings alike without a marker. A generic effect operation, by contrast, now carries illegal_type_parameters -- mapped to ErrorTree -- and agrees. History: 47 over 22 fixtures at flix-spec 0.75.8; 56 over 28 at 0.77.1 (the 47 unchanged, 9 in new negative fixtures); 55 after the v0.77.0 grammar work; 56 after the law removal, which also lifted depth 63% -> 65%; 55 and 67% with the illegal_type_parameters marker.

diagnostic_conformance.comment: Current: 8 divergences, 139/147 fixtures agree, accept/reject only. The adapter reports one `tree-sitter.ParseError` per unit containing an ERROR node, a MISSING token or a recovery marker; no diagnosticMappings translates that name, so kind and line stand down -- an ERROR spans the recovery region, not the reference's error token. Parse-phase evidence only, as flix-spec's canonical set is lexer and parser errors alone. Seven are units the reference rejects and this grammar accepts: one by design (a spaced package `::`, parsed as Parser2 builds it) and six grammar gaps (unterminated block comment, unterminated string interpolation, `static` as a name, a misplaced doc comment, an operator signature in a trait, an anonymous class). The eighth runs the other way: operator-error.flix, which the reference accepts and this grammar rejects. History: first measured at 9; the illegal_type_parameters marker brought the generic effect operation into agreement.

source_invariants.comment: document-shape passes. The two vocabulary checks stand down because a projection map is in play, and token-accounting and token-positions stand down because this adapter emits no token text -- tree-sitter's named-node view has no Flix tokenization behind it. A structural profile, stated rather than implied.
